Villain.name: Villain
Villain.description:
People who use their Quirks for crime, from muggers, shoplifters and street thugs to armed robbers, smugglers, hired muscle and the rare ideological killer. Heroes stop them, the police arrest them, and the worst end up in Tartarus. Most work alone or in small crews; brokers such as Giran sell them jobs, hideouts, forged IDs and black-market support gear. At the start of the year the League of Villains is tiny: Tomura Shigaraki, Kurogiri and thugs hired through brokers.

Villains have reasons: money, revenge, ideology, addiction, fear or the thrill of breaking rules. Small-timers rob, run and hide; organized ones scout, plan and recruit; a dangerous few go looking for heroes. In a fight most use their Quirks without restraint, grab hostages, wreck property to cover an escape and flee when a pro arrives; a cornered small-timer often gives up. A villain-path player meets them as contacts, rivals, employers and threats, and their loyalty has to be earned. To most of them a hero or student is a target or an obstacle, and a civilian is a victim or leverage.

## Generating New NPCs
Tomura Shigaraki, Kurogiri, Stain (the Hero Killer), Giran and every villain who joins the League later are canon NPCs: never generate a stand-in for them. A generated villain is a petty criminal, gang member, smuggler, small-time broker or hired thug, usually no match for a pro, and knows nothing of the League's plans. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting the region (foreign only for visitors from abroad), never a canon character's name or family name; a street alias is optional. The Quirk has a clear scope and a real limit or cost. A heteromorph body never marks someone as a villain.

## Visual Description
Adults with no shared uniform: street clothes, hoodies, work clothes, masks, scarves, caps and cheap or black-market gear. Mutant features always show. No capes, glowing eyes, blood or gore unless the record states them, and no text or logos.
